# PLAN — iteration 1
## Current state assessment
The baseline passes the frozen simulation and reports 101 LUTs, 128 FFs, 6 DSP48s, setup WNS −9.981 ns, and hold WHS +0.171 ns. The critical register-to-register path has 16 logic levels, including a five-DSP cascade followed by carry-chain addition, so timing closure is the immediate objective; the top’s known latency is 1 cycle.

## Hypothesis
Explicitly balancing the eight signed products into a pairwise sum tree should shorten the DSP cascade and reduce the critical path enough to improve setup slack, while preserving the one-cycle behavior and reset semantics.

## Instruction for generator
Keep the `d[0:7]` shift register, synchronous active-high reset, registered `y_out`, and `// @latency 1` unchanged. Replace the left-associated eight-term sum assigned to `y_out` with an explicit balanced tree: form four adjacent product pairs, then two pair sums, then the final sum, using signed 32-bit intermediates and preserving the original 32-bit result semantics for every supported coefficient parameter. Check reset and impulse behavior, signed high-bit inputs, and overflow; the expected benefit is fewer serial DSP stages on the path to `y_out`, with any LUT/FF/DSP changes measured after routing.
